title: Self-Optimizing Expert Advisors in MQL5 (Part 20): Causality Regularization With Time-Lagged Independent Components Analysis (3)
text:
Introduction
This article addresses the problems faced by practitioners attempting to suppress noise in financial market data while preserving useful information to empower their trading decisions. Distinguishing market noise from a true signal is a materially challenging task; failing to address this problem meaningfully can result in unreliable trading strategies that lose investors' capital and confidence.
Our current time-lagged ICA solution learns to approximate the independent component manifold from financial market data and uses these approximations to forecast a manually defined surrogate target. Below, we shall outline two potential blind spots associated with our current solution:
The quality of our forecast is implicitly determined by the characteristics of the hand-crafted target we implemented. This makes it difficult to discern if we have obtained the best performance possible. Should algorithmic traders have to toil indefinitely, generating thousands of hand-crafted targets to be confident in their current performance levels?
The geometric distance between the current ICA manifold and future smoothed returns could be vastly greater than the distance between the future ICA manifold and future smoothed returns. Our current approach may place an unnecessary strain on the model by forcing the model to bridge a large mathematical gap. Alleviating this geometric gap may enhance model reliability.
In concrete terms, we will show that the ICA algorithm can be seen as a valuable coordinate transformation that allows us to forecast in a possibly richer, low-dimensional space that may have less noise than the direct approach of forecasting returns immediately from the approximate ICA manifold. This layered piecewise approach has practical benefits for algorithmic traders:
In machine learning, you must validate that the target is a function of the observations. Because the ICA manifold is directly constructed from observed price levels, the relationship our models are learning might be better exposed, which in turn may result in improved performance.
Using the ICA algorithm as its own target generator creates a feedback loop that has the potential to better align our manifold model and the two forecasting models.
After learning to reconstruct future smoothed returns from forecasted independent components, we then had to address the challenge of understanding the relationship between our algorithmic surrogate targets and the smoothed market returns we intended to forecast. To achieve this we explored two possible solutions:
Learn the average effect brought about by the independent component that grew the most.
Employ Shapley Additive Explanations to learn how changes in the components affect the target.
These two approaches gave us a balanced picture of the relative importance of each component and the market regimes associated with growth in these components. We compiled these statistics to render refined noise signals that look for regime switches, misaligned trade entries, and disagreements between the average effect of the dominant independent component and the expected effect of our current spectral cluster.
Getting Started in MQL5
To get started with our analysis, we will first write a handy script to fetch the historical data we need for our analysis. This script has been used extensively in all our discussions so far and will be familiar for our returning readers. However, for any new readers joining our discussion, we will give a brief outline of the functionality of the script.
The script accepts important user settings that configure the number of historical bars fetched and the period and mode of the moving average indicator used. The script then fetches the corresponding market data and its historical 5-day lag. These lags are copied for both raw prices and for the technical indicator. This produces a large matrix with 49 columns and as many rows as you specified.
Once you have created the script, drag and drop it onto your symbol of choice with your intended time frame already selected. For our discussion, we will employ the EURUSD pair on the daily time frame.

Analyzing Our Market Data in Python
We can now start analyzing our historical market data. Our goal here is to demonstrate that the future growth in the ICA manifold can be forecasted with higher accuracy than our current surrogate target. We will compare our accuracy in classifying changes in smoothed returns against our ability to classify changes in the ICA manifold and empirically observe changes in performance. We will now create a new column to denote which independent component has grown the most over our forecast horizon. This is simply calculated as the argmax of the manifold group from our training set. Note that we are not interested in the largest value but the column that contains the largest value. Setting the axis parameter to 1 means that we are performing this check on each row of our training set.

Now that we have demonstrated that the ICA manifold generates richer surrogate targets than we can manually engineer over the same space of time, let us now observe if our ability to reconstruct future smoothed returns is better than the performance levels we would obtain from the direct approach. To ensure a fair comparison, we will tune all the models we are interested in. We have 5 models to optimize. The first 3 models are part of our iterative solution. The last 2 models will be used as benchmarks that our chain of models should outperform. The first benchmark captures the results we would have obtained by forecasting smoothed returns using our moving average indicator readings as inputs. The second benchmark reflects the performance we would have reached if we forecasted smoothed returns immediately from approximated ICA components. Each of the 5 models will be allowed 100 optimization iterations over the training set before being evaluated on the out-of-sample test set.

Understanding How Our Forecasted Components Fit In With Our Strategy
So far, we have demonstrated that the ICA algorithm can be used as an algorithmic generator of rich surrogate targets. We observed that by forecasting the growth in these components, our model can reconstruct the intended target, with greater accuracy than what we were capable of attaining with our previous direct approach. Now, we wish to understand how these forecasted components interact with the rest of our strategy. This task can be broken down into 2 primary objectives:
Understanding the relative importance of each independent component and the effect that component has on our ability to reconstruct the final target.
Searching for interactions between our ICA manifold and the spectral clusters we identified in our previous discussion.
Our first task may be answered by Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). Afterward, we will search for interactions and dependencies between our ICA manifold and the spectral clusters in our dataset by building a covariance matrix between the two.
Obtaining SHAP Explanations
SHAP explanations are a mathematically principled tool for understanding the inner workings of a machine learning model. The SHAP algorithm was originally inspired by developments in the mathematical field of game theory. SHAP explanations offer us robust model-agnostic explanations of global and local model behavior. We have covered the SHAP algorithm in detail in our previous discussion on "The Disagreement Problem: Diving Deeper into The Complexity Explainability in AI." For readers who may want a refresher, a link to that article is provided
here
. To get started, we will import the SHAP library and the surrogate model we wish to explain.

shap

sklearn.neighbors

We want to understand our model's behavior over the entire training set. To do this, we will first define a utility function that will return the predicted probabilities our classifier assigns to each training instance. Then we will store the median values of our ICA forecasted components. These median values are used by the SHAP algorithm to compare the effect each component has, in light of the average effect brought about by that component. These median values are then passed to our SHAP explainer, along with the utility function we designed to return the expected probability of price levels rising given the forecasted ICA components. Finally, we pass our SHAP explainer the entire training set to obtain both global and local explanations.

Global SHAP explanations help us understand the importance of each feature the model was trained on, whereas local explanations give us a case-by-case breakdown of each prediction our model made and how the input values affected its prediction. Let us first obtain a global explanation of our final model that is responsible for reconstructing the smoothed market return, given forecasted growth across ICA components.
In Figure 6 below, we have made a bee-swarm plot of the global importance of each ICA component. The components are arranged with the most important feature at the top and the least important feature at the bottom. In our case the growth in the second, eighth, and third ICA components was estimated to be the top 3 most important inputs by the SHAP explainer.
It is interesting to note that the models that consistently grew the most in our ICA manifold were not necessarily the most important features identified by the SHAP explainer.
The SHAP explainer also attempts to help us understand what happens to our model's output when each of the inputs is above or below its average. Blue points indicate low feature values, while pink points indicate high feature values. The direction of influence that these extreme values had is represented by the points' position along the x-axis. Data points that pushed the model's output higher are on the right of the x-axis, while points on the left of the x-axis pushed the model's predictions lower.
Generally speaking, most of the points on the right-hand side of the x-axis are blue, while most of the pink points are on the left-hand side. This may suggest that high values in the independent components influence the model to forecast lower returns, and the opposite appears true of low input values.

Our trading strategy is growing in complexity. It may be possible that there are rich relationships and interactions unexpectedly taking shape between ICA components we have optimized and the spectral clusters we identified in our previous discussion. If such interactions exist, it would be challenging for us to directly observe these patterns due to the high number of dimensions involved. Fortunately, there exist a myriad of statistical algorithms that allow us to automatically identify relationships in data. One of these algorithms is implemented by calculating a covariance matrix between the two. To do this, we will first reproduce the ideal clustering setup we learned from our previous discussion.

Нет чёткого условия типа 'если Manifold 2 растёт > X и кластер = 8, то BUY', только общие описания архитектуры и аналитики. Нужны данные, которых нет у спот-форекса: в коде используется `iMA(..., PRICE_HIGH/LOW/OPEN/CLOSE)` с последующим `CopyBuffer` и построением матрицы из 49 столбцов, включая лаги OHLC и MA по каждому типу цены — но в спот-форексе (особенно в MQL5 на реальных счетах) нет гарантированно доступных исторических OHLC-баров с точностью до тика; более того, `iMA` на `PRICE_OPEN`/`PRICE_LOW`/`PRICE_HIGH` в спот-форексе часто возвращает некорректные или отсутствующие значения, так как эти цены не являются котировками спреда, а вычисляются из тиков — их нет в стандартных спот-исторических данных MetaTrader (только Close и иногда Open, но не гарантированно High/Low для всех баров).
judge.summary: Статья представляет исследование применения Time-Lagged ICA и многоуровневого машинного обучения для повышения точности прогнозирования сглаженных доходностей на форексе. Однако она не содержит детерминированного торгового правила: нет чётких условий входа, используются данные будущих баров (lookahead), а требуемые OHLC-данные неприменимы в условиях спот-форекса.
